title_en: Supreme People's Court Releases Five Typical Cases of Food and Drug Disputes
keywords_en: contract dispute; sales contract; guarantee; court-announced five food and drug disputes
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Publishes Five Typical Cases of Food and Drug Disputes

Case 1

Sun Yinshan v. Nanjing Auchan Supermarket Co., Ltd. Jiangning Branch — Dispute over Sales Contract

— A consumer who knowingly purchases expired food and requests the business operator to pay ten times the price of the food as compensation is supported by the court

(1) Basic Facts

On May 1, 2012, the plaintiff, Sun Yinshan, purchased 15 packs of "Yutu Brand" sausages from the defendant, Auchan Supermarket Co., Ltd. Jiangning Branch (hereinafter referred to as Auchan Supermarket), of which 14 packs valued at RMB 558.6 had expired (the plaintiff knew this). After checking out at the cashier, Sun Yinshan went directly to the service counter to claim compensation. As negotiations failed, Sun Yinshan filed a lawsuit with the Nanjing Jiangning District People's Court, requesting that Auchan Supermarket pay compensation of ten times the selling price, totaling RMB 5,586.

(2) Judgment

The court held that Article 2 of the Law on the Protection of Consumer Rights and Interests provides: "Where consumers purchase or use commodities or receive services for daily consumption, their rights and interests shall be protected by this Law; where this Law is silent, they shall be protected by other relevant laws and regulations." In this case, Sun Yinshan performed the act of purchasing commodities, and Auchan Supermarket failed to provide evidence that his purchase was for production or resale. Moreover, the plaintiff Sun Yinshan claimed compensation because he purchased expired food, which is the exercise of a statutory right. Therefore, Auchan Supermarket's defense that Sun Yinshan was not a consumer could not be established.

Food sellers have a statutory duty to ensure food safety and shall promptly remove from shelves food that does not meet safety standards. However, Auchan Supermarket still sold sausages beyond their expiration date, which constitutes a failure to perform a statutory duty and shall be deemed as selling food that it clearly knew did not meet food safety standards. In such circumstances, consumers may simultaneously claim compensation for losses and ten times the price, or may claim only ten times the price. Sun Yinshan's request that Auchan Supermarket pay ten times the selling price is an act of the party exercising its own rights and shall be supported. In accordance with Article 96 of the Food Safety Law, the court ordered the defendant Auchan Supermarket to pay the plaintiff Sun Yinshan compensation of RMB 5,586. This judgment has now taken legal effect.

Case 2

Hua Yan v. Beijing Tianchao Storage and Supermarket Co., Ltd., 26th Branch, and Beijing Tianchao Storage and Supermarket Co., Ltd. — Dispute over Personal Rights and Interests

— Where a consumer suffers personal injury due to consuming substandard food and requests the seller to pay medical expenses and ten times the purchase price as compensation in accordance with the law, the People's Court shall support such claim

(1) Basic Facts

On May 6, 2009, the plaintiff, Hua Yan, purchased hawthorn slices twice from the defendant, Beijing Tianchao Storage and Supermarket Co., Ltd., 26th Branch (hereinafter referred to as the 26th Branch), paying RMB 10 and RMB 6.55 respectively (for evidence collection). While eating the hawthorn slices, a hawthorn pit cracked her molar. On the same day, Hua Yan went to the hospital for treatment and had the damaged molar extracted. For this, Hua Yan paid a total of RMB 421.87 for the extraction and treatment, RMB 4,810 for denture fitting, RMB 6.4 for transportation, and RMB 15.8 for photocopying. Later, when Hua Yan sought to negotiate the matter with the 26th Branch, she was refused. Hua Yan then called 12315 to file a complaint. After mediation by the Tuanjiehu Branch of the Beijing Chaoyang District Consumer Association (hereinafter referred to as the Tuanjiehu Consumer Association), no agreement was reached. She then filed a lawsuit with the Beijing Chaoyang District People's Court, requesting that the defendants pay RMB 421.87 for extraction and treatment, RMB 4,810 for denture fitting, RMB 6.4 for transportation, RMB 15.8 for photocopying, RMB 17 for the purchase price plus ten times the initial purchase price as compensation totaling RMB 117, and RMB 8,000 for moral damages. The Tuanjiehu Consumer Association issued a statement to the court confirming that the hawthorn slices purchased by Hua Yan showed defects even when the packaging was intact. During the trial, Beijing Tianchao Storage and Supermarket Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Tianchao Company) provided a joint sales contract, relevant licenses of the hawthorn slice producer, and inspection reports for the hawthorn slices, proving that the hawthorn slices it sold met product quality requirements. Upon investigation by the court, before the incident in this case, Hua Yan had previously sought medical treatment for the same tooth, and after treatment, the tooth wall became thin and more susceptible to external force.

(2) Judgment

The Beijing Second Intermediate People's Court held on second instance that, according to the national safety and hygiene standards for preserved fruits, soft hawthorn slices should be free of impurities. The hawthorn slices sold by Tianchao Company contained very hard hawthorn pits, which did not meet the relevant national food safety and hygiene standards, and should be deemed to have quality defects. The seller of substandard food shall bear full liability for the harm caused by such substandard food. Hua Yan's own tooth walls were thin, but she was not at fault for the harm in this case, and the liability of the tortfeasor is not reduced thereby. From the statement issued by the Tuanjiehu Consumer Association, the defect in the hawthorn slices was discoverable even when the outer packaging was intact. Therefore, the product seller sold the product knowing that it had safety issues and shall pay the consumer ten times the purchase price as compensation. Given that Hua Yan did not suffer severe mental harm, her claim for moral damages was not supported in accordance with the law. Accordingly, the court, pursuant to Article 96 of the Food Safety Law, ordered Tianchao Company to pay Hua Yan medical expenses of RMB 5,231.87, transportation expenses of RMB 6.4, and a refund of the purchase price plus ten times the purchase price as compensation totaling RMB 116.55.

Case 3

Pi Minmin v. Chongqing Far Eastern Department Store Co., Ltd., Chongqing Wulingshan Zhenwang Food Development Co., Ltd., et al. — Dispute over Product Liability

— Where a food product has quality issues causing harm to a consumer, the consumer may simultaneously sue both the producer and the seller

(1) Basic Facts

On May 5, 2012, Pi Minmin purchased 10 boxes of "Wulingshan Zhenjia Yanbao" produced by Chongqing Wulingshan Zhenwang Food Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Zhenwang Company) from Chongqing Far Eastern Department Store Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Far Eastern Company), at a unit price of RMB 448 per box, totaling RMB 4,480. Each box of "Wulingshan Zhenjia Yanbao" contained several individual pre-packaged foods, namely matsutake mushrooms, delicious boletus, yellow boletus, sliced shiitake mushrooms, old man's head, tea tree mushrooms, green bar fungi, ball cap fungi, and Oriental Magic Soup Mix. The outer packaging of each box of "Wulingshan Zhenjia Yanbao" indicated storage methods, ingredients, consumption methods, net content, product implementation standards, production license, production date, shelf life, and the address and telephone number of the manufacturer, but the Oriental Magic Soup Mix did not list its original ingredients. Zhenwang Company originally used Q/LW7-2007 as its enterprise production standard. After that standard expired, the company failed to renew it in a timely manner for various reasons, and continued to mark Q/LW7-2007 on the packaging as its product production standard. In September 2012, the company submitted a statement explaining the expiration of the enterprise standard to the Quality and Technical Supervision Bureau of Shizhu Tujia Autonomous County, Chongqing, and in October 2012, after filing with the Chongqing Municipal Health Bureau, it released the current product standard Q/LW0005S-2012. Pi Minmin believed the food she purchased was substandard and filed a lawsuit with the Chongqing Jiangbei District People's Court, requesting that Far Eastern Company refund the purchase price of RMB 4,480, and that Zhenwang Company pay five times the price as compensation, totaling RMB 22,400.

(2) Judgment

The court of first instance ruled: (1) Far Eastern Company shall refund Pi Minmin the purchase price of RMB 4,480 within ten days from the effective date of the judgment. (2) Pi Minmin's other claims were dismissed.

The court of second instance held that food producers and business operators shall engage in production and business activities in accordance with the Food Safety Law of the PRC and relevant laws and regulations, be responsible to society and the public, ensure food safety, accept social supervision, and bear legal liability in accordance with the law. The focus of the dispute between the parties in this case was whether the food in question had food safety and other issues, and the applicable law and legal liability in this case. First, whether the food in question had food safety and other issues: (1) The "Wulingshan Zhenjia Yanbao" food produced by Zhenwang Company failed to file its food safety enterprise standard in accordance with the notice of the health department, and continued to implement the expired Q/LW7-2007 enterprise standard, violating relevant mandatory food standards; (2) The "Oriental Magic Soup Mix" in the food was a pre-packaged food, and its label did not indicate ingredients or ingredient lists and product standard codes, which did not comply with the relevant provisions of the Food Safety Law on labeling of pre-packaged foods; (3) The phrase "I am the best for home health" on the packaging was text beyond what is required by national standards for commodity packaging, had characteristics of advertising, and should be governed by the Advertising Law; this phrase constituted an absolute term prohibited by the state and was illegal. Second, the applicable law and legal liability in this case: The Food Safety Law is a special law vis-a-vis the Tort Liability Law. As this case involves food safety issues, the Food Safety Law and relevant laws and regulations shall apply. Based on the above findings of issues with the food in terms of food safety standards, packaging, and advertising, the producer and business operator of the food shall bear corresponding legal liability in accordance with relevant laws and regulations on food safety. The Chongqing Food Safety Management Measures is a local administrative regulation of Chongqing, which may be applied by reference if it does not conflict with laws and regulations. Pi Minmin's request to apply Article 67 of those Measures, to return the food and pay five times the purchase price as compensation, was consistent with the spirit of Article 96 of the Food Safety Law, and should be supported. Accordingly, the court ruled: (1) Affirmed the first instance judgment's first item; (2) Set aside the first instance judgment's second item; (3) Zhenwang Company shall pay the appellant Pi Minmin compensation of RMB 22,400.

Case 4

Cong Lisong v. Beijing Panjiayuan Outpatient Department of Ciming Health Examination Management Group Co., Ltd. — Dispute over Product Seller Liability

— Where a business operator provides goods or services with fraudulent conduct, and a consumer requests the operator to return the goods and pay compensation of one times the price, the People's Court shall support such claim

(1) Basic Facts

On June 2, 2012, the plaintiff, Cong Lisong, saw an advertisement for "Shenqi Oral Liquid" in the Legal Evening News, titled "New Breakthrough in Treatment of Advanced Tumors," which stated that the absorption and utilization rate of this drug could be several times higher than that of traditional Chinese medicine; below the advertisement, the exclusive sales address was listed as "Ciming Integrated Chinese and Western Medicine Pharmacy," 100 meters north of the west gate of the Tumor Hospital at Zuo'anmen on the East Second Ring Road. To treat his aunt who had cancer, Cong Lisong purchased one box of "Shenqi Oral Liquid (Xiao'ai Ping Oral Liquid)" at the Beijing Panjiayuan Outpatient Department of Ciming Health Examination Management Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as the Panjiayuan Outpatient Department) on the same day, priced at RMB 450, which bore the mark "National Drug Approval Number Z20050778." He later discovered that this drug was a prescription drug that must be used under the guidance of a physician, and no such guidance was provided at the time of sale. The Beijing Municipal Drug Administration's "Announcement on Illegal Drug Advertisements" issued in March 2012 stated: "2. Thirty-three drug varieties were involved in illegal advertisements, with actions including releasing advertisements without approval and unauthorized alteration of approved advertisement content. Among them, two drugs with the indicated names 'Jieshitong Tea' and 'Shenqi Oral Liquid' had serious illegal advertisements. The drug with the indicated name 'Shenqi Oral Liquid' claimed in its advertisements to be developed using 'atomic micro-breaking nucleus therapy,' containing 'micro-tubule blocker' and 'specific activating factor,' capable of killing and eliminating tumor cells, preventing tumor recurrence, spread, and metastasis. The advertisements for these drugs contained exaggerated indications and unscientific efficacy guarantees, seriously misleading and deceiving consumers." The "Summary Table of Illegal Drug Advertisements" attached to the "Announcement on Illegal Drug Advertisements" issued by the Beijing Municipal Drug Administration from April to June 2012 included "Shenqi Oral Liquid," and the business operators indicated after it included "Ciming Integrated Chinese and Western Medicine Pharmacy." Cong Lisong believed that the Panjiayuan Outpatient Department exaggerated the drug's indications and efficacy in its advertisements, seriously misleading and deceiving consumers, and therefore filed a lawsuit with the Beijing Chaoyang District People's Court, requesting a refund of the purchase price of RMB 450, compensation of RMB 450, payment of RMB 9,099 for lost time, and RMB 1 for moral damages.

(2) Judgment

The court of first instance held that the drugs sold by the Panjiayuan Outpatient Department were qualified, Cong Lisong's claim that the Panjiayuan Outpatient Department had engaged in fraudulent conduct lacked sufficient evidence, and the court could not be convinced that Cong Lisong had a legitimate reason for purchasing such goods. Although he submitted the original receipt issued by the Panjiayuan Outpatient Department, the court still could not be convinced of his consumer status. Therefore, the court dismissed Cong Lisong's claims. Dissatisfied with the judgment, Cong Lisong appealed to the Beijing Second Intermediate People's Court, requesting that the second instance amend the judgment to support his first instance claims.

The court of second instance held that where a consumer's lawful rights and interests are harmed because a business operator provides goods or services through false advertising, the consumer may claim compensation from the business operator. Where a business operator provides goods or services with the act of publishing false advertisements, deceiving and misleading consumers, thereby harming the lawful rights and interests of consumers who purchase goods or receive services, the business operator shall, at the consumer's request, increase compensation for the losses suffered, with the increased compensation amount being one times the price of the purchased goods or the cost of the received services. In this case, Cong Lisong sued the Panjiayuan Outpatient Department on the grounds that the "Shenqi Oral Liquid" he purchased involved false advertising, requesting that it bear compensation liability. The court of second instance supported his claim, and the Panjiayuan Outpatient Department shall bear compensation liability for Cong Lisong's reasonable losses. Cong Lisong's claims for a refund of the purchase price of RMB 450 and increased compensation of RMB 450 had a legal basis, and the court supported them. Cong Lisong's claim for lost time was not supported because he did not provide sufficient evidence. Cong Lisong's claim for moral damages had no factual or legal basis and was also not supported. In accordance with Articles 39 and 49 of the Law on the Protection of Consumer Rights and Interests, and Article 170(1)(2) of the Civil Procedure Law, the court ruled: set aside the first instance judgment; the Panjiayuan Outpatient Department shall refund Cong Lisong the purchase price of RMB 450 and pay increased compensation of RMB 450; dismiss Cong Lisong's other claims.

Case 5

Wang Quan v. Oriental Kidney Disease Hospital — Dispute over Compensation for Mail-Order Drug Purchase

— Where a hospital publishes illegal advertisements in the media to induce consumers to purchase drugs, and after taking the drugs ineffectively, the consumer discovers that the advertisements were untrue, the People's Court shall support the consumer's request for double refund of the drug purchase price

(1) Basic Facts

Oriental Kidney Disease Hospital (hereinafter referred to as the Kidney Disease Hospital) published an advertisement in Sichuan Daily titled "New Hope for Treating Kidney Disease and Uremia: Holistic Root Therapy of Oriental Kidney Disease Hospital." The advertisement introduced the characteristics, efficacy, and treatment methods of the holistic root therapy using Chinese medicine for kidney disease and uremia. After seeing this advertisement, Wang Quan consulted the Kidney Disease Hospital, which replied to his inquiry letter, stating that its hospital's holistic root therapy could fundamentally treat kidney disease. From October 2003 to October 2004, Wang Quan ordered by mail "Dongfang Shengsheng San," "Dongfang Kidney Disease Capsules," and "GS Series Holistic Treatment Device" worth a total of RMB 20,180 from the Kidney Disease Hospital. After taking the purchased drugs and using the treatment device, his condition did not improve. In February 2005, Wang Quan reported to the Weifang Municipal Administration for Industry and Commerce, Shandong Province, that the Kidney Disease Hospital's advertisements were untrue. The administration replied that it had initiated an investigation and dealt with the hospital's illegal advertisements for medical and internal preparations in violation of the Advertising Law, and ordered it to stop publishing the illegal advertisements. Accordingly, Wang Quan filed a lawsuit with the Jiangyang District People's Court of Luzhou, Sichuan Province, requesting that the Kidney Disease Hospital and Sichuan Daily return double the medical expenses, totaling RMB 40,360. During the first instance, Wang Quan withdrew his lawsuit against Sichuan Daily.

(2) Judgment

The court of first instance held that the content of the advertisement published by the Kidney Disease Hospital and the letters it sent to Wang Quan implied that the treatment could cure kidney disease, misleading Wang Quan into accepting treatment from the Kidney Disease Hospital, causing him to incur unnecessary treatment expenses. This misleading conduct harmed Wang Quan's lawful rights and interests, and the hospital shall bear civil liability. Wang Quan's claim for double refund of medical expenses was lawful, and the court supported it. In accordance with Article 122 of the General Principles of the Civil Law and Article 49 of the Law on the Protection of Consumer Rights and Interests, the court ordered the Kidney Disease Hospital to compensate Wang Quan RMB 40,360, with the first instance litigation costs borne by the Kidney Disease Hospital. Dissatisfied with the first instance judgment, the Kidney Disease Hospital appealed to the Luzhou Intermediate People's Court, arguing that it had not harmed Wang Quan's lawful rights and interests, and requested that the court set aside the original judgment and dismiss Wang Quan's claims.

The court of second instance held that the Kidney Disease Hospital's act of publishing false advertisements in the newspaper violated Article 14 of the Advertising Law, which provides that advertisements shall not contain unscientific assertions or guarantees of efficacy, nor shall they include content indicating cure rates or effectiveness rates. Wang Quan, misled by the medical advertisement, purchased drugs and treatment equipment from the Kidney Disease Hospital, thereby suffering economic losses. The advertiser, the Kidney Disease Hospital, shall bear compensation liability. According to Article 38 of the Advertising Law, advertising operators and publishers shall bear joint and several liability. However, Wang Quan voluntarily withdrew his lawsuit against Sichuan Daily, which was an exercise of his litigation rights. This case is not a damages lawsuit based on personal injury caused by drugs or treatment equipment, but rather a case where illegal advertisements misled Wang Quan, causing him to purchase drugs and treatment equipment from the Kidney Disease Hospital in reliance on its ability to cure kidney disease, and after treatment, the advertised effects were not achieved, resulting in economic losses. In accordance with Articles 39 and 49 of the Law on the Protection of Consumer Rights and Interests and Article 153 of the Civil Procedure Law then in effect, the court ruled in February 2007 to dismiss the appeal of Oriental Kidney Disease Hospital and affirm the original judgment.
